questions.question: Your startup's AWS bill has climbed to $500K/month and leadership wants it down 40% in 90 days without degrading SLOs. You lead a 6-person platform team. Walk through your plan.
questions.title: Scenario: Cutting a $500K/month AWS Bill 40% in 90 Days Without Breaking SLOs
questions.direct_answer: **First 30 days: measure and kill obvious waste.** Set up tagging enforcement, Cost and Usage Report → Athena dashboards, Kubecost for K8s attribution, and per-team cost visibility. Kill the free wins: unattached EBS, old snapshots, idle RDS replicas, DEBUG log retention, forgotten dev environments, missing VPC endpoints. Expected: **~10–15% reduction**, zero SLO risk. **Days 30–60: compute rightsizing and commitment strategy.** Rightsize pods/tasks using p95 utilization, set Karpenter with Spot + on-demand mix, buy **Compute Savings Plans** covering 70% of steady baseline, move log retention from 90 to 14 days with S3 archive, fix log-level discipline. Expected: **another ~15–20%**, careful SLO monitoring. **Days 60–90: architectural shifts.** Migrate steady high-RPS workloads off Lambda to ECS Fargate; introduce scale-to-zero on non-prod + off-hours shutdowns; S3 Intelligent-Tiering + lifecycle; consolidate observability vendors or tune Datadog metrics. Expected: **remaining 5–10%**. Throughout: **cost dashboards per team**, **weekly waste reviews**, **SLO monitors per service**, and **rollback plan** if anything regresses. Communicate clearly: this isn't a one-shot cut, it's installing a **FinOps practice** that sustains. Biggest risks: Spot interruption hitting stateful workloads, aggressive log-retention hiding an incident investigation, commitment overshoot if architecture shifts.

interviewer_intent.soft_skills: Prioritization, leadership, stakeholder communication, risk management, cost discipline
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Random cuts; missing observability and data transfer; no SLO monitoring; commitment over-buy
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: Phased plan with concrete targets, governance install, SLO safeguards, specific AWS services, risk communication

sections.title: The Scenario and What the Interviewer Is Testing
sections.content:
**Situation**
- AWS bill: $500K/month, growing 15% month-over-month
- Leadership mandate: 40% reduction in 90 days, **no SLO regressions**
- Team: 6 platform engineers; product teams operate their own services
- Current state: mixed K8s (EKS) + Lambda + some ECS, RDS/Aurora, S3, DynamoDB, Datadog + CloudWatch logs, no consistent tagging, no cost dashboards, one engineer doing ad-hoc Cost Explorer queries
- Culture: engineers don't know their service's cost; finance panics; no waste reviews

**What's being tested**
- Do you have a **systematic framework** (FinOps) vs. ad-hoc cuts?
- Can you sequence high-leverage, low-risk work first?
- Do you factor **observability + data transfer** (often 30–40% of overlooked costs)?
- Can you **protect SLOs** while cutting?
- Do you build **durable governance** or just a one-shot cut that regresses?
- Can you **communicate risk** honestly to leadership?
- Do you avoid anti-patterns: Spot on stateful, over-committed Savings Plans, aggressive log cuts that blind incident response?

**What good looks like at day 90**
- $300K/month (40% cut) with SLOs intact or improved
- Cost dashboards per team; engineers see their spend
- Tagging enforced; weekly waste reviews running
- Savings Plans at ~70% baseline coverage; Spot with Karpenter
- Observability bill down 50–70%; log retention 14 days + S3 archive
- Data transfer optimized with VPC endpoints and topology-aware routing
- FinOps practice installed — this is sustainable, not one-shot

sections.title: Days 0–30: Visibility + Zero-Risk Quick Wins (~15%)
sections.content:
Goal: see where the money goes, capture easy savings, install the metrics that will guide the next 60 days.

**Visibility (week 1)**
- Enable **Cost and Usage Reports (CUR)** to S3
- Build **Athena + QuickSight** dashboards: spend by service, by team (via tags), week-over-week, anomaly flags
- Install **Kubecost** or **OpenCost** on EKS for per-namespace / per-pod attribution
- Publish a **cost leaderboard** per team — visibility alone drives 5% reduction

**Tagging enforcement (week 1–2)**
- Define mandatory tags: `team`, `service`, `env`, `cost-center`, `owner`
- Write AWS Config rules to flag untagged resources
- Tag existing resources via Terraform / AWS Resource Groups Tag Editor
- Policy: new resources without tags get quarantined (not created) via SCP + Terraform pre-commit

**Zero-risk quick wins (week 2–4)**
- **Unattached EBS volumes** — `aws ec2 describe-volumes --filters Name=status,Values=available` → delete after 7-day review. Often $5–20K/month.
- **Old snapshots** — retention policy: keep 7 daily + 4 weekly + 12 monthly; delete the rest. Often $3–10K/month.
- **Orphaned load balancers / Elastic IPs** — unattached, still billing
- **Idle RDS replicas / instances** — flag anything with <5% CPU for 30 days
- **Duplicate snapshots, old AMIs** — cleanup scripts
- **Dev/staging forgotten for 60+ days** — auto-terminate policy
- **CloudWatch Logs**:
  - Retention >30 days on DEBUG → move to 14 days + S3 archive
  - Often **the single biggest line item** after compute
  - Audit `println`/`logger.debug` spam; fix in code
- **VPC endpoints** for S3, DynamoDB, Secrets Manager, SSM → avoid NAT egress. $0.045/GB saved immediately on affected traffic.
- **NAT Gateway consolidation** — one per AZ shared across services, not per team
- **Orphaned ECS tasks, old Lambda versions** — retention policies

**SLO safeguards**
- Install Datadog / CloudWatch SLO monitors before cutting anything
- Baseline latency p95/p99, error rates, availability per service
- Alert on regressions immediately

**Expected outcome**: $50–75K/month saved, **zero SLO risk**, full visibility in place. Team morale boost from visible wins.

sections.title: Days 30–60: Compute Rightsizing + Commitment (~15–20%)
sections.content:
Now tackle the big line items with moderate-risk work.

**Compute rightsizing (EKS)**
- Use Kubecost / VPA recommendations based on 14-day p95
- Most pods are 2–4× overprovisioned in memory, 3–5× in CPU
- Set requests close to p95; limits somewhat above
- Validate with synthetic load + production canary (1 pod at new size, observe)
- Roll per namespace, not globally; give teams agency
- **Java JVM tuning**: confirm `-XX:MaxRAMPercentage=75`, `-XX:+UseContainerSupport`
- **Java startup**: AppCDS in containers cuts startup 30–50%, reduces warm-up pod count

**Compute rightsizing (ECS / Lambda)**
- ECS tasks: AWS Compute Optimizer recommendations; rightsize CPU/memory
- Lambda: memory = CPU; sometimes higher memory is **cheaper** (faster → fewer GB-seconds) — measure
- Lambda Power Tuning tool to find optimal memory per function

**Node strategy: Karpenter + Spot**
- Replace Cluster Autoscaler with **Karpenter** (better binpacking, faster, cheaper)
- Node pool: 30% on-demand baseline + 70% Spot for stateless workloads
- PodDisruptionBudget on critical workloads; Spot interruption handler (AWS Node Termination Handler)
- Stateful (databases, stateful sets) stay on on-demand
- Expected compute savings: **30–50%** on the Spot-eligible portion

**Savings Plans / Reserved Instances**
- Analyze 6 months of steady baseline
- Buy **Compute Savings Plans** (flex across instance family/region) covering **70% of baseline**
- 1-year, no upfront — flexible enough to change
- Leave peak + headroom on on-demand
- For RDS steady: Reserved DB instances (1-year no upfront)
- **Don't overcommit** — if architecture shifts (move to Fargate, rearchitect to serverless), stranded commitment is pain

**Observability tuning**
- **CloudWatch logs**: retention 90 → 14 days; S3 archive for long-term. $10–30K/month savings.
- **Datadog metrics**: cardinality audit — any metric with userId/requestId tags? Fix it. Cardinality explosion is silent $$.
- **Datadog APM traces**: sampling 100% → 5% (100% on errors) — no visibility loss for debugging, massive cost drop
- **Datadog custom metrics**: audit list; delete ones unused
- **Log levels**: DEBUG only in non-prod; INFO in prod; ERROR with context

**Data transfer fixes**
- Identify top NAT egress via VPC Flow Logs → Athena
- Add missing VPC endpoints
- Co-locate chatty services in same AZ (topology spread constraints)
- CDN for hot S3 content (CloudFront)

**SLO safeguards**
- Rightsizing regression? Scale back that namespace; diagnose
- Spot interruption impact? More on-demand baseline; better PDB
- Keep SLO dashboards live in every meeting

**Expected outcome**: another $75–100K/month. Some SLO tension, caught by monitors, rolled back where needed.

sections.title: Days 60–90: Architectural Shifts + Governance (~5–10%)
sections.content:
Goal: close the remaining gap with architectural optimizations; install durable governance.

**Lambda → ECS Fargate migration for steady high-RPS**
- Audit Lambda spend: any function with sustained >10 req/sec is often cheaper on ECS Fargate
- Package as container; deploy on existing Fargate infrastructure
- Keep true event-driven / low-RPS on Lambda (it earns its keep there)
- Expected savings: **40–60%** on migrated workloads

**Storage lifecycle**
- **S3 Intelligent-Tiering** for buckets with mixed access
- **Lifecycle rules**: archive logs older than 30 days to Glacier; delete after retention window
- Delete incomplete multipart uploads globally
- Compress objects where reasonable (zstd for logs)
- Expected savings: **30–50%** on storage

**Database optimization**
- Move variable-load DBs to **Aurora Serverless v2** (auto-scale capacity)
- Right-size RDS: many are 4× provisioned
- **Aurora I/O-Optimized** for I/O-heavy
- Stop non-prod RDS nights/weekends (cron to bypass 7-day auto-start)
- Archive cold data (older than 1 year) from Postgres to S3 / Data Lake
- Reduce read replicas to SLO-driven minimum

**Non-prod off-hours shutdown**
- Scheduled shutdown weeknights + weekends for dev / staging
- Typically saves **50–70%** on non-prod compute
- Auto-start on PR open or manual trigger

**Governance install (crucial for sustainability)**
- **OPA / Gatekeeper / Kyverno** on K8s: block pods without resource requests, reject untagged workloads, ban instance types above size X
- **AWS Service Control Policies** block expensive regions, large instance types without approval
- **Terraform Sentinel / OPA** on IaC for policy as code
- **Budgets per team**: alerts at 50/80/100%
- **AWS Cost Anomaly Detection** → Slack
- **Weekly waste review**: 30 min platform team + product team reps; close-loop fixes

**FinOps culture embed**
- Cost per request / per tenant metrics in each service's dashboard
- Cost discussed in sprint retros and PRDs
- FinOps champion per product team — platform team coaches
- Celebrate savings publicly; no shaming

**Observability consolidation (harder / optional)**
- Datadog + CloudWatch duplication? Consolidate
- Self-host Prometheus + Grafana + Loki for non-critical metrics if volume is huge
- Evaluate usage-based plans vs enterprise commit

**Expected outcome**: final $25–50K/month. Total: $150–200K/month saved (30–40%). Governance installed so next quarter's bill doesn't regress.

sections.title: Trade-offs, Risks, and Senior Communication
sections.content:
**Spot interruption risk**
- Stateless services: fine with proper PDB, readiness probes, 2-min warning handler
- Stateful: stay on on-demand; RDS / stateful sets / single-replica services
- CI runners, batch jobs: excellent Spot candidates
- Mitigation: mixed instance types, multiple AZs, graceful shutdown

**Savings Plan commitment risk**
- Buy too much → stranded commitment if architecture shifts
- Buy too little → miss discounts
- Middle path: 70% of stable baseline; 1-year no upfront for flexibility; re-evaluate quarterly
- Document forecast assumptions; revisit if architecture changes

**Aggressive observability cuts**
- Cutting logs too deep blinds incident response
- 14-day hot + S3 archive gives cheap long-term access via Athena
- Keep ERROR/WARN full fidelity; sample INFO/DEBUG
- Don't cut APM during active incidents; sample more aggressively in steady state

**Rightsizing risk**
- Too tight → OOMKills, throttling, latency spikes
- Validate with canary pod; monitor GC, p99, memory pressure
- Roll per namespace; don't big-bang across platform

**Cost vs reliability**
- Minimum replicas for redundancy, even if CPU says 1 is enough
- Multi-AZ redundancy costs inter-AZ traffic — can't eliminate all of it
- SLO trumps cost always — monitor both in every change

**Engineering time ROI**
- Prioritize big levers; don't sink 2 engineers on 3% savings for 6 weeks
- Automate right-sizer suggestions; let teams apply
- Platform team provides paved path; product teams own usage decisions

**Common failure modes**
1. **Random cuts without measurement** — SLO regressions, finger-pointing
2. **No tagging first** — can't attribute or target
3. **Cutting Datadog before understanding queries** — blind incident investigation
4. **Overcommit savings plans** — architectural shift later makes them stranded cost
5. **Spot on stateful workloads** — data corruption or outage
6. **Scale-to-zero on user-facing prod** — cold-start SLO breach
7. **One engineer crusade** — team doesn't own it, regresses after they burn out
8. **Cutting dev environments engineers need** — velocity drops, revolt
9. **No governance after cuts** — bill regrows next quarter
10. **Overselling savings to leadership** then under-delivering — credibility lost

**Senior communication to leadership**
- **Phase plan with targets**: 15% → 30% → 40%, with SLO guardrails
- **Risk register**: what could go wrong, mitigation
- **Metrics dashboard**: weekly savings vs target, SLO status
- **Non-negotiables**: no SLO breach, no commitment overbuy
- **Sustainability**: install FinOps, not just a cut — avoid "we'll do this again next year"
- **Ask for support**: policy enforcement (SCP), tagging mandate, team accountability
- **Credit the team**: product teams who cut their own spend deserve recognition

**Senior communication to engineers**
- **Frame as engineering metric**, not finance witch-hunt
- **No shaming**: waste is normal, finding it is good
- **Training**: what things cost, how tagging works, how to read dashboards
- **Celebrate wins**: Slack announcements, demos, team leaderboards
- **Empower**: give them tools (Kubecost, right-sizer) rather than tickets

**What I'd tell a peer senior**
- Don't chase the shiny: big levers first, dashboards early, SLOs always
- The goal isn't a one-shot cut; it's a practice that sustains
- Governance is the only reason the bill doesn't regrow next quarter
- Work with product teams, not around them — they own their services
- Measure weekly; celebrate weekly; adjust weekly

sections.title: Key Points
sections.content:
- **Systematic 40% cut in 90 days is achievable** with FinOps framework + SLO guardrails
- **Days 0–30**: visibility (CUR, Kubecost, tagging), zero-risk quick wins (~15%)
- **Days 30–60**: rightsize + Karpenter + Spot + Savings Plans + observability tuning (~15–20%)
- **Days 60–90**: architectural shifts (Lambda→Fargate, S3 lifecycle, Aurora Serverless, off-hours) + governance (~5–10%)
- **Tagging enforcement first** — can't optimize what you can't attribute
- **SLO monitors in place before cutting anything**; rollback on regression
- **Observability is often top-3 cost**; tune log retention + metric cardinality + trace sampling
- **Data transfer is hidden**: VPC endpoints, NAT consolidation, same-AZ topology
- **Spot for stateless only**; on-demand baseline + Spot via Karpenter
- **Savings Plans ~70% baseline**; don't overcommit
- **Governance is the durability play**: OPA, SCP, budgets, weekly waste review
- **Risks to communicate**: Spot interruption, commitment overbuy, aggressive log cuts
- **FinOps as culture**: cost is an engineering metric, not finance's problem
- **Celebrate + empower**; don't shame engineers or teams

sections.title: How to Answer This Verbally
sections.content:
I'd run a 90-day FinOps-driven plan in three phases with SLO guardrails throughout.

**Days 0–30: visibility and quick wins (~15%)**
- Enable Cost and Usage Reports → Athena → QuickSight dashboards per team
- Install Kubecost on EKS for per-namespace attribution
- Enforce tagging: team, service, env, cost-center, owner
- AWS Config flags untagged; Terraform pre-commit blocks new untagged
- Publish cost leaderboard — visibility alone drives 5%

*Zero-risk quick wins*
- Unattached EBS volumes and old snapshots
- Orphaned ELBs, Elastic IPs, old AMIs
- Idle RDS instances and replicas
- Forgotten 60-day dev environments
- CloudWatch Logs: cut 90-day retention to 14 days + S3 archive
- VPC endpoints for S3, DynamoDB, Secrets Manager — avoid NAT egress
- NAT Gateway consolidation
- Orphaned ECS tasks, old Lambda versions
- Install SLO monitors before cutting anything

**Days 30–60: rightsize and commit (~15–20%)**

*Compute rightsizing*
- Use Kubecost / VPA 14-day p95 recommendations
- Most pods 2–4x overprovisioned
- Roll per namespace with canary validation
- Java: -XX:MaxRAMPercentage=75, UseContainerSupport, AppCDS for startup
- ECS tasks via AWS Compute Optimizer
- Lambda via Lambda Power Tuning — sometimes higher memory is cheaper

*Node strategy*
- Replace Cluster Autoscaler with Karpenter
- 30% on-demand baseline + 70% Spot for stateless
- PDB + Node Termination Handler
- Stateful on on-demand
- 30–50% savings on Spot-eligible

*Commitment*
- Compute Savings Plans covering 70% of steady baseline
- 1-year, no upfront — flexible
- Reserved DB for steady RDS
- Don't overcommit — architecture shifts create stranded cost

*Observability tuning*
- CloudWatch log retention 90 → 14 days + S3 archive — often 10–30K/month
- Datadog metric cardinality audit — userId/requestId tags explode cost
- APM sampling 100% → 5% + 100% on errors
- Custom metrics audit and prune
- Log levels: DEBUG only non-prod

*Data transfer*
- VPC Flow Logs → Athena to find top NAT egress
- Missing VPC endpoints
- Co-locate chatty services in same AZ (topology spread)
- CloudFront for hot S3 content

**Days 60–90: architectural + governance (~5–10%)**

*Lambda → ECS Fargate for steady high-RPS*
- Any Lambda with sustained >10 req/sec often cheaper on Fargate
- 40–60% savings on migrated workloads
- Keep true event-driven on Lambda

*Storage lifecycle*
- S3 Intelligent-Tiering for mixed access
- Lifecycle rules: Standard → IA → Glacier → Deep Archive
- Delete incomplete multipart uploads
- Compress logs and analytics

*Database*
- Aurora Serverless v2 for variable load
- Right-size RDS
- Aurora I/O-Optimized for I/O-heavy
- Stop non-prod nights/weekends
- Archive cold data to S3
- Read replicas to SLO minimum

*Off-hours shutdown*
- Non-prod scheduled shutdown — 50–70% savings
- Auto-start on PR or manual

*Governance install*
- OPA / Gatekeeper / Kyverno on K8s
- AWS Service Control Policies
- Terraform Sentinel on IaC
- Per-team budgets with 50/80/100% alerts
- AWS Cost Anomaly Detection → Slack
- Weekly waste review — 30 min, close-loop fixes
- FinOps champion per product team

**SLO safeguards throughout**
- SLO dashboards per service, live in every meeting
- Rollback policy on any regression
- Canary rightsizing before namespace rollout
- Keep on-demand baseline; don't all-in on Spot

**Trade-offs and risks**
- Spot interruption: stateless only, mixed instances, PDB, graceful shutdown
- Savings Plan commitment: 70% baseline, re-evaluate quarterly; document forecast
- Aggressive log cuts: keep ERROR full, sample INFO/DEBUG, don't cut during incidents
- Rightsizing: canary, monitor GC/p99/memory, roll per namespace
- Cost vs reliability: SLO trumps cost always
- Engineering time ROI: big levers first, automate rightsizer

**Failure modes to avoid**
- Random cuts without measurement
- No tagging first
- Cutting Datadog before understanding queries
- Overcommit Savings Plans
- Spot on stateful
- Scale-to-zero on user-facing prod
- One-engineer crusade
- Cutting dev envs engineers need
- No governance after cuts
- Overselling to leadership then under-delivering

**Communication**

*To leadership*
- Phase plan: 15% → 30% → 40% with SLO guardrails
- Risk register + mitigation
- Weekly dashboard: savings vs target, SLO status
- Non-negotiables: no SLO breach, no commitment overbuy
- Ask for support: SCP policy, tagging mandate, accountability
- This is a practice install, not a one-shot cut

*To engineers*
- Engineering metric, not finance witch-hunt
- No shaming; waste is normal, finding is good
- Training on costs, tagging, dashboards
- Celebrate wins publicly
- Empower with Kubecost, right-sizer tools

**Bottom line**
- 40% in 90 days is achievable with disciplined phasing
- The win isn't just the cut — it's the FinOps practice that sustains
- Governance is the only reason bill doesn't regrow next quarter
- Product teams own their usage; platform centralizes rates and policy
- SLOs protected, celebrate wins, measure weekly
